about: How the outcome web runs on the new core (src/core2/modules/outcome-web.ts). The links themselves, their sizes, shapes, lags and sources are data/research/outcome-web/links.json; each place outcome's real starting level is data/research/outcome-web/place-outcome-bases-2024.json. This file holds only what those leave open: when the web runs each month, the outcomes it keeps that have no per-state base file, the records the engines already keep that it reads, and who must provide each missing measure.

schedule.why: World-metrics writes the town's economic row on the 2nd of each month; the web reads it the next day.

worldBases.about: Owner, Oct 27: every statistic starts realistic, not real, unless it is in law. A kept outcome's published state level is the center; each world moves it once by its own offset, drawn from the world's seed at Start (seeded generation of the starting world, never an actor's outcome). A percent moves relative to its nearer bound, so it stays between 0 and 100.

spreadShare.citation: How far a world's state level of an outcome sits from the published one, as a share of it: about the typical year-to-year change plus survey margin of state outcome measures (ACS one-year state margins of error run 1% to 5% of the estimate; state violent crime, overdose and homelessness rates move 5% to 15% a year, FBI UCR, CDC WONDER, HUD PIT).

worldBases.lawMeasuresWhy: Rates set in law stay as the real starting law (owner, Oct 27). The property-tax rate is the ACS effective rate, held here until the CTO rules whether it is law (docs/reports/real-statistics-in-play-2026-10-27.md).

lawsModule.why: OPUS-GOV's laws module keeps every level's law rows (series, jurisdiction, value, effectiveDate) and announces each phase as a law-took-effect event; a law measure is 1 when any level's latest row in force says yes.

births.rate.unit: index, 100 at the place's own starting birth rate (the renewal engine's natality rates by age)

source.citation: The renewal engine's natality rates (data/research/renewal/natality-2023.json, natality-2024.json) are the base; the links move them proportionally.

crime.assault.unit: assault victimizations (aggravated and simple) per 1,000 persons 12 and older a year

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf): aggravated assault 4.7 plus simple assault 14.4, as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 NCVS assault rates; no state rate is recorded, so every place starts from the national figure.

crime.burglary.unit: burglary victimizations per 1,000 households a year

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 NCVS household burglary rate; no state rate is recorded, so every place starts from the national figure.

crime.property.unit: property victimizations per 1,000 households a year

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization, 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), table 2, total property crime (burglary, trespassing, motor vehicle theft and other theft), legacy instrument.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 NCVS total property crime rate; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

crime.robbery.unit: robbery victimizations per 1,000 persons 12 and older a year

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Criminal Victimization 2024 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/cv24.pdf), as recorded in data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 NCVS robbery rate; no state rate is recorded, so every place starts from the national figure.

crime.vandalism.unit: index, 100 at the place's own starting vandalism rate

source.citation: Vandalism is not an NCVS category (data/research/crime/roadmap-r38-victimization-reporting.json); the web keeps it as an index on the place's own start, which is how the links size it (a proportional change).
source.estimatedFrom: Index form: 100 is where the place began; the links move it proportionally.

health.mortality-55-64.unit: deaths per 100,000 people ages 55 to 64 a year

source.citation: National Center for Health Statistics, Mortality in the United States: Provisional Data, 2025 (VSRR No. 44, https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/vsrr/vsrr044.pdf), table of final 2024 age-specific death rates, ages 55 to 64.
source.estimatedFrom: The national final 2024 rate; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

health.youth-firearm-deaths.unit: firearm deaths per 100,000 people ages 1 to 19 a year

source.citation: CDC WONDER mortality data, 2021 to 2023, as reported by America's Health Rankings, Firearm Deaths among Children, ages 1 to 19 (https://www.americashealthrankings.org/explore/measures/firearm_deaths_children).
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2021 to 2023 rate for ages 1 to 19; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

health.youth-firearm-suicide.unit: firearm suicides per 100,000 people ages 10 to 19 a year

source.citation: Johns Hopkins Center for Gun Violence Solutions and Center for Suicide Prevention analysis of final CDC data, Gun Suicides in the U.S., 2023 (reported by Stateline, https://stateline.org/2025/06/27/gun-suicides-in-us-reached-record-high-in-2023/): 1,252 gun suicides ages 10 to 19 in 2023; rate 3.0 for white youth and 3.3 for Black youth.
source.estimatedFrom: About 3 per 100,000, between the two reported group rates of 3.0 and 3.3; the all-youth rate itself was not in the report text. Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

housing.eviction.unit: eviction cases filed per 100 renter households a year

source.citation: Eviction Lab, Eviction Tracking System 2024 report (https://evictionlab.org/ets-report-2024/): filing rate 7.6 percent across the tracked cities and full states.
source.estimatedFrom: The rate across the places Eviction Lab tracks, not a count of the whole country. Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

housing.rent.unit: index, 100 at the place's own starting rents (the housing engine's leases); the links move it proportionally and the engine renews each lease by the change

source.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2023 1-year estimates, table B25064, median gross rent (national $1,406 a month).
source.estimatedFrom: Each place starts at its own rents, which the housing engine records on its leases; the web holds only the proportional change its links put on them, so no national dollar level stands in for a place's rent.

housing.home-value.unit: index, 100 at the place's own starting home values (the housing engine's owned homes); the links move it proportionally and the engine values each home, and prices each sale, by the change

source.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020-2024 5-year estimates, table B25077, median value of owner-occupied housing units (the housing engine's opening values, dated mid-2022).
source.estimatedFrom: Each place starts at its own home values, which the housing engine records on its dwellings; the web holds only the proportional change its links put on them, so no national dollar level stands in for a place's home value. The measure the births links read, housing.home-prices, is the engine's median home value itself and already includes this change.

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Prisoners in 2023 (https://bjs.ojp.gov/document/p23st.pdf), as reported by USAFacts: 43 federal prisoners per 100,000 residents.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2023 rate, taken from a secondary report of the BJS tables; it is a national figure for every place.

justice.low-level-arrests.unit: arrests for disorderly conduct, drunkenness, liquor law violations, curfew and loitering violations, vagrancy and drug possession per 1,000 residents a year

source.citation: FBI Crime Data Explorer, arrest data, 2024: the sum of the 12 monthly arrest rates of the six offenses for the agencies that reported in each state (https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/arrest/state/{ST}/{offenseCode}?type=counts&from=01-2024&to=12-2024; offense codes 290, 280, 270, 330 and 300 read Oct. 25, 2026, and drug possession as the sum of codes 156, 157, 158, 159 and 160 read Oct. 26, 2026), kept with every offense's counts and coverage in data/research/justice/low-level-arrests-2024.json.
source.estimatedFrom: Five of the six categories are the FBI's own series (SOURCED). Drug possession is ESTIMATED (laws lead ruling, Oct. 25, 2026): the FBI has no single drug possession series, so it is the sum of five, and arrests booked only as 'Drug Abuse Violations' (no split between sale and possession) are left out. The data file tags each category.

justice.low-level-arrests.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 rate for all reporting agencies (the same source's United States row, the six categories together); the source holds no arrests in these categories for this place, so it starts from the national figure and the web moves it from there.

justice.pretrial-detained.unit: people held in local jails without a conviction per 100,000 residents

source.citation: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Jail Inmates in 2023 preliminary release (https://bjs.ojp.gov/preliminary-data-release-jails-2023): 467,600 of 664,200 people in local jails at midyear 2023 were unconvicted.
source.estimatedFrom: 467,600 divided by the 2023 U.S. resident population of about 335 million; the count includes people held for reasons other than a pending charge. Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

labor.low-wage-jobs.unit: percent of workers paid less than $15 an hour

source.citation: Economic Policy Institute press release on 2022 wages: more than 20 million workers, 15 percent of the workforce, paid less than $15 an hour (https://www.epi.org/press/new-report-finds-the-lowest-paid-workers-have-seen-historically-fast-wage-growth-since-2019/).
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2022 share from Current Population Survey wage data; the 2023 national total was not found. Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

labor.undocumented-employment.unit: percent of the labor force that is unauthorized immigrant workers

source.citation: Pew Research Center estimate for 2022 from American Community Survey data: 8.3 million unauthorized immigrant workers, 4.8 percent of the U.S. labor force (cited in Economic Policy Institute, FAQ on unauthorized immigrants, https://files.epi.org/uploads/FAQ-Unauthorized-Immigrants-v5.pdf).
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2022 share, taken from a secondary citation of the Pew estimate; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

labor.us-born-employment.unit: employment-population ratio of native-born people 16 and older, percent

source.citation: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Foreign-Born Workers: Labor Force Characteristics, 2024 (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/forbrn.nr0.htm): native-born employment-population ratio 59.3 percent.
source.estimatedFrom: The national 2024 ratio; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

labor.wages.unit: average hourly earnings of private employees, dollars

source.citation: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, Average Hourly Earnings of All Employees, Total Private (CES0500000003), seasonally adjusted, December 2024 (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/data/CES0500000003).
source.estimatedFrom: The national December 2024 figure; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

school.hispanic-enrollment.unit: percent of public school students who are Hispanic

source.citation: National Center for Education Statistics, Common Core of Data, fall 2022 public school enrollment by race and ethnicity: Hispanic 28.9 percent of 49.6 million students (https://nces.ed.gov/learn/press-release/nces-data-show-public-school-enrollment-held-steady-overall-fall-2022-fall-2023).
source.estimatedFrom: The national fall 2022 share; Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

voting.youth-turnout.unit: percent of citizens ages 18 to 29 who voted in the presidential election

source.citation: U.S. Census Bureau, Voting and Registration in the Election of November 2024 (P20-590, https://www2.census.gov/library/publications/2026/demo/p20-590.pdf), table 2: 23,540 thousand voted of 46,380 thousand citizens ages 18 to 29.
source.estimatedFrom: Computed from the table's counts for ages 18 to 29, because its age rows begin at 18 to 29; the link is researched for ages 18 to 24. Every place starts from the national figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

voting.local-turnout.unit: percent of registered voters who voted in the most recent mayoral election

source.citation: Zoltan Hajnal and Avi Green, Big Cities - Tiny Votes? America's Urban Voter Turnout (Yankelovich Center for Social Science Research, December 2024, https://yankelovichcenter.ucsd.edu/_files/reports/Big-Cities-Tiny-Votes.pdf): "Across the 50 cities, mayoral turnout averages only 37.1 percent" of registered voters in each city's most recent mayoral election.
source.estimatedFrom: The average of the 50 largest cities' most recent mayoral elections, as a share of registered voters; towns and counties differ, and off-cycle elections average 26.2 percent in the same report. Every place starts from this figure; no place-level series is recorded, so each starts at the national level and the web moves it from there.

household.income.record: world-metrics months.medianHouseholdEarningsMinor (the middle earning household's yearly earnings), in thousands of dollars

housing.home-prices.record: world-metrics months.medianHomeValueMinor (the housing engine's typical owned home), in tens of thousands of dollars

housing.rent-to-income-pct.record: world-metrics months.rentToEarnings (a year of the typical rent against the typical household's earnings), as a percent

housing.eviction-orders.record: world-metrics months.evictionOrdersLastMonth (the housing engine's judgments in the month before): the engine's own records, read by links that start from evictions; the kept housing.eviction is only the factor the engine applies

crime.violent-victimization-index.record: crime months.violentIndex (robberies and assaults per person 12 and older the victimization records expect, 100 at the place's first month)

crime.reported-per-capita.record: crime months.reportedPerResident (victimizations reported to police, a year, per resident)

household.poverty-pct.record: world-metrics months.povertyShare (people in households whose yearly pay and awards are under the Census poverty line for their size, children and eldest member, named plus counted by weight), as a percent

disaster.severe.record: the disasters engine's news events (hazard.disaster) for the town: the highest severity (0 to 1, the homes FEMA inspected as damaged per resident on the ramp in src/core2/data/disasters/severity.json) among disasters that began since the world opened, within the last ten years

housing.property-tax-rate.record: the property tax rate in force for the town (the budgets module's law row the housing engine bills owners by), as a percent of home value

tax.state-corporate-rate-in-force.record: the state corporate income tax rate in force for the town (the laws module's state row of corporate-income-tax), in percent of taxable corporate income; 0 where the state levies none

budget.parks-added-pct.record: gov-measures budget.parks-added-pct: the city's parks line above its Census base this fiscal year, in percent (the budgets module's budget row in force)

budget.highways-added-pct.record: gov-measures budget.highways-added-pct: the town's highway spending above its Census base this fiscal year, in percent (each government's highways line in the budgets module, by the town's share of it)

police.officers-per-1000.record: public-safety months.officersPer1000 (sworn officers per 1,000 residents: the state's recorded rate times the town's police service, its police lines against where they began the year)

budget.schools-added-pct.record: the schools lines of the town's city and county budgets in force (the budgets module's rows the school engine's spending measure reads), together, above their Census base for the fiscal year, as a percent

program.snap-maximum-change-pct.record: the SNAP one-person maximum allotment in force (the federal snap-maximum law row), against the one in force at the opening, as a percent

budget.healthAndHospitals-added-pct.record: the town's share of the health and hospitals line across the governments that carry it, above its Census base (every bill and act that changed it), as a percent

budget.welfareAndMedicaid-added-pct.record: the town's share of the welfare and Medicaid line across the governments that carry it, above its Census base (every bill and act that changed it), as a percent

budget.higherEducation-added-pct.record: the town's share of the higher education line across the governments that carry it, above its Census base (every bill and act that changed it), as a percent

press.local-newspaper.record: the press module's outlets table: how many of the town's own local newspapers have closed (their business books in the finance ledger carry a closing date), counted; zero while they all publish

measureOwners.about: Who provides each measure the web is waiting on. A measure an engine already keeps but sets itself (rent, home prices, evictions, unemployment, employment) waits on that engine reading the web's factor for it (outcomeWebFactor).
